findings.title: A rerun destroys earlier results: logs and JSON are overwritten, and nothing stops a second STAGE=test
findings.problem: The shell `> $OUT/eval_<stage>.log` empties the log as soon as gpu_gate.sh starts, before the gate even lets the job run. RunRecord writes the --out JSON with status "running" when it starts, so it replaces the old eval_val.json or eval_test.json at once. Nothing checks for an existing eval_test.json before the test branch runs.
findings.failure_scenario: The first test run finishes and writes eval_test.json with status ok. Someone then relaunches STAGE=test by mistake, or to 'retry' after a later tail/grep problem. eval_test.log is emptied right away, and eval_test.json becomes a 'running' record with metrics {} the moment eval_seg starts. The only copy of the test numbers is gone, and getting them back means a second test run. This already happened once on validation: the 20:18:31 relaunch overwrote eval_val.log, and the office_0 numbers now survive only as a hand copy (logs/eval_val_partial_2013.log, lines marked [transcript]).
findings.evidence: replica_tab1.sh:59 `--out "$OUT/eval_test.json" > "$OUT/eval_test.log" 2>&1`. Simulated with RunRecord: the file exists with status 'running' inside the with-block and ends as 'failed' with metrics {}. The current /home/thanhnc/gauss_ws/data/uags_results/tab1/eval_val.log starts at '[gpu_gate] 2026-09-29 20:18:31 waiting' and holds only 84 KB of gate lines, so the 20:13 run output is lost. stage_val.log line 125: 'restart 2026-09-29 20:18:31 at cc65f08'.
findings.fix: (1) Give each launch its own log: TAG=$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S); write eval_${STAGE}_${TAG}.log and point eval_${STAGE}.log at it with ln -sf. Or append with >> after a header line (date, git rev-parse HEAD, env). (2) In the test branch, refuse to run if eval_test.json exists, unless FORCE_TEST_RERUN=<reason> is set, and log that reason. (3) In eval_seg.main, refuse an --out that already holds a record with status ok or running, unless --overwrite is given. Or write the run to <out>.<run_id>.json and copy it to --out only on success.

findings.title: The test stage only checks that eval_val.json exists; the file on disk now is a failed record with no betas
findings.where: scripts/replica_tab1.sh:29-46 (test maps built first), 56 (existence check); scripts/replica_views.sh:27; scripts/eval_seg.py:488-493 (None settings only warns), 425 (betas_used raises only after load_scene)
findings.problem: `[ -f "$OUT/eval_val.json" ]` accepts any record, including one with status failed or running. The check also runs AFTER the loop that fits and maps all 6 test scenes. With an empty betas file, eval_seg only warns that no fit settings were recorded. It then loads the first test scene (LSeg tokens on its evaluation frames, all rows frozen) and only after that crashes in betas_used.
findings.failure_scenario: If STAGE=test is launched now, or after a val rerun that crashes, the script spends hours of GPU time and about 8 GB of disk mapping the test scenes. The test evaluation then crashes on room_0 with 'rows [...] have no usable fitted beta'. That is a failed test run on record, and the test maps are built from whatever code is checked out at that moment.
findings.evidence: python3 -c "...json.load(open('.../tab1/eval_val.json'))" -> status 'failed', start 20:13:45, end 20:16:30, metrics keys []. Simulated a failed RunRecord, then eval_seg.load_betas(p) -> {} and load_fit_settings(p) -> None. replica_views.sh:27 uses the same existence-only check.
findings.fix: Move the check to the top of the test branch, before the mapping loop. Replace it with a Python check that the record has status == 'ok', that metrics.betas holds every Table I row (ours_P0/P1/P2, ours_scalar, averaging, normlift, viewcount, css, 2d_features), and that beta_fit_settings is present. In eval_seg, make a missing beta_fit_settings or an empty betas dict an error, not a warning, whenever --betas is given. Apply the same check in replica_views.sh and replica_tab3.sh.

findings.title: A crash in the middle of the test evaluation loses every finished scene, which forces a second test pass
findings.problem: Per-scene results go into the run record only after ALL scenes are done (`for k, v in out.items(): rec.add(k, v)` at the end of run()). If scene k crashes, scenes 1..k-1 are gone from the JSON. They survive only as printed lines in a log that the next launch overwrites.
findings.failure_scenario: The validation eval already crashed twice with CUDA OOM on the shared GPU (15:18 and 20:16). If the test eval crashes on office_2, the numbers for room_0, room_1 and office_1 have already been printed and seen. The rerun must evaluate them again, which breaks the run-test-once rule for those scenes.
findings.evidence: eval_seg.py:541-549 fills res in memory. rec.add runs only at lines 551-553. RunRecord supports flush() (runlog.py docstring: 'written ... on every flush()'), but eval_seg never calls it per scene. The 20:16 val crash left eval_val.json with metrics {} although office_0 was fully evaluated.
findings.fix: After each scene: rec.add('scenes', res); rec.add('betas', out['betas']); rec.flush(). Add --resume <partial.json>. It loads the finished scenes from a partial record only if betas, beta_fit_settings, config_sha256 and the git code hash all match, and evaluates only the missing scenes. Record in the report which scenes were resumed.

findings.title: The paper says CSS gets the full vocabulary at mapping time; the code gives it only the classes present in the test frames' ground truth
findings.where: papers/main.tex:643-644 ('CSS receives the full vocabulary at mapping time'); usplat/baselines.py:34-37 (docstring: 'all classes ... never the classes present in a test scene'); scripts/run_mapping.py:104-120 (css_vocabulary) and 228-230
findings.problem: run_mapping.css_vocabulary reads the label maps of the scene's EVALUATION sequence (Sequence_2, stride 10) at mapping time. It builds the CSS Dirichlet over exactly the classes present there: 16-28 of the 101 classes. The paper text and the baselines.py docstring both describe the opposite.
findings.failure_scenario: A reviewer reads that CSS works over the full 101-class vocabulary. In fact, at mapping time CSS gets the test-scene class list taken from test labels. The comparison is still fair, because the open-vocabulary rows use the same class list as their queries at evaluation time. The setup text is simply wrong, and the docstring would mislead anyone who checks the code.
findings.evidence: stage_val.log: 'CSS vocabulary: 24 classes present in .../office_0/Sequence_2' and '21 classes present in .../room_2/Sequence_2'. A CPU check over all 8 scenes comparing full-resolution Sequence_2 classes with eval_seg's downscaled query set: office_0 24/24, room_2 21/21, room_0 28/28, room_1 24/24, office_1 22/22, office_2 21/21, office_3 26/26, office_4 16/16. The sets match exactly (no CSS-only class) and there are 0 unknown label pixels.
findings.fix: Change the paper sentence to: 'CSS receives, at mapping time, the classes present in the scene's evaluation frames (the query set of the other rows); the open-vocabulary rows need these classes only at query time.' Fix the baselines.py (d) docstring to match. Do not change the code: the val maps already use this rule.

findings.title: '180 mapping frames' is wrong: the near-duplicate filter keeps 176-180 frames per scene
findings.where: papers/main.tex:593, 693, 775 (and the views figure's M=180); scripts/run_mapping.py:183-200 (select, defaults --kf-trans 0.05 --kf-rot 5); scripts/replica_tab1.sh:37-40 (no kf flags)
findings.problem: run_mapping drops a frame when its pose moved less than 5 cm AND less than 5 degrees since the last kept frame. Every scene but one loses 1-4 of its 180 frames. The paper states 180 frames and uses M=180 as the full map. Also, the 3DGS geometry is fit on 157 of the 180 frames (23 held out for PSNR). The text only says the map is fit 'on the mapping frames'.
findings.failure_scenario: The setup text and the views figure axis state a frame count that the pipeline does not use. For office_1 the field is built from 176 frames, not 180.
findings.evidence: Map logs: office_0 'keyframes used 179', room_2 'keyframes used 179'. Replaying select() on traj_w_c.txt (CPU) gives kept/180: office_0 179, room_2 179, room_0 179, room_1 178, office_1 176, office_2 178, office_3 179, office_4 180. Example: office_0 frame 295 dropped (3.2 cm, 2.6 deg). The fit_room_2.log meta says n_train 157, n_test 23.
findings.fix: Cheapest fix: change the text to 'every 5th frame of Sequence_1 (180 frames; near-duplicate poses, <5 cm and <5 deg from the previous kept frame, are skipped: 176-180 per scene)' and 'the full map (all kept frames)'. Also say that the 3DGS map is fit on 157 of them. The alternative is to pass --kf-trans 0 --kf-rot 0 in replica_tab1.sh and replica_views.sh, but then both val fields must be rebuilt and the betas refit before the test run.

findings.title: Field files carry no code version, and existing fields are reused without a check, so val and test fields can come from different code
findings.where: scripts/run_mapping.py:319-323 (saved dict: field, pca, config, timing, field_config, extractor, baselines, css_class_ids; no git/code hash); scripts/replica_tab1.sh:36 (reuse if the file exists); scripts/eval_seg.py:247-251 (checks only the extractor name); usplat/extractors/lseg.py:293-307 (UAGS_LSEG_STRIDE/FLIP/SCALES/HALF env overrides, not recorded)
findings.problem: The temperatures are fit on the val fields: office_0 built at 5b21781, room_2 at 5e8c51e. The test fields will be built later, from whatever code is checked out. Attempt 06 (P3) is being implemented right now. Nothing records or compares the mapping code, the FieldConfig defaults, or the LSeg options between the two sets. eval_seg compares only the extractor name. fit_gs.py does record git and code_sha256 in its map meta; run_mapping does not.
findings.failure_scenario: Say P3 or any other fix changes vmf_field/baselines/FieldConfig defaults before STAGE=test. The test fields then carry different statistics from the val fields that the betas were fit on, and Table I mixes two methods. No file shows this afterwards. The same happens silently if UAGS_LSEG_* or DOWNSCALE is set differently in the test shell.
findings.evidence: torch.load(..._lseg.pt, mmap=True) keys: ['baselines','config','css_class_ids','extractor','field','field_config','pca','timing']. There is no git entry. The val configs differ only in paths, and field_config is identical. `git diff 5b21781 HEAD --stat -- usplat scripts` shows run_mapping/gpu_reserve changes only, so the two sets still match TODAY. By contrast, map meta shows office_0 git '408dc8a+dirty' and room_2 '260afb7' with code_sha256 recorded.
findings.fix: In run_mapping, save code=usplat.runlog.git_state(...) (commit, dirty, code_sha256), plus the LSeg options (token_stride, flip, scales, half), into the field file. In eval_seg.load_scene, collect these per scene. In --betas mode, refuse to run when a test field's mapping code hash or its config (minus paths) differs from the fields named in the betas record. That record must then store its fields' hashes, so add them to beta_fit_settings. As a minimum, have replica_tab1.sh STAGE=test print git rev-parse HEAD and git status --short into the stage log, and refuse to run with a dirty tree.

findings.title: make_tables.py does not match the tab:replica layout and does not check its input
findings.where: scripts/make_tables.py:20-29, 48-66; papers/main.tex tab:replica (the \midrule before Ours, and the P2 row with \multicolumn{2}{c}{as P0})
findings.problem: (a) The script emits no \midrule between CSS and Ours P0. (b) For Ours P2 it prints mIoU and Acc numbers, but the paper has \multicolumn{2}{c}{as P0}. (c) It prints 'same predictive as averaging' for both NormLift rows without checking that the normlift and averaging metrics are equal. (d) std is the population std (scene_stats unbiased=False), and neither the paper nor the script output says so. N appears only in a comment, as a set over rows, so a cell with fewer scenes (NaN dropped) is not flagged. (e) It does not check that the JSON is a finished test record: it would print eval_val.json numbers (N=2) under the 'test, N=6' caption.
findings.failure_scenario: The generated rows cannot be pasted as-is: the P2 row and the midrule differ from the paper. If a future change makes NormLift's buffer differ from averaging's, the table would still claim the predictive is the same. If run on the wrong file, the output has val numbers under the test caption.
findings.evidence: Ran tab1() on a synthetic 6-scene summary (scratchpad fake_test.json). Output: 8 rows in the right order and labels, no \midrule line, and 'Ours P2 (adaptive $\beta$) & \checkmark & 44.0{...} & 32.8{...} & ...' with numbers in the mIoU/Acc cells. Units are correct: mIoU/Acc/ECE/AURC/AUSE x100 with 1 decimal, Brier x100, NLL with 2 decimals. seg_eval.py:613-621 uses population std.
findings.fix: Emit '\midrule' before the first Ours row. For ours_P2, assert that |mIoU/Acc(P2) - mIoU/Acc(P0)| < 1e-9 per scene and print '\multicolumn{2}{c}{as P0}'. For the NormLift rows, assert that their predictive summary equals averaging's, else raise. Assert status == 'ok', 'betas_path' present (not a fit), and summary n == 6 for every printed cell. Write 'std over scenes (population), N = 6' in the caption.

findings.title: The paper says the coverage floor is set on validation; the code fixes it at 0.5 beforehand
findings.where: papers/main.tex:621-622; scripts/replica_tab1.sh (TAU_COV=${TAU_COV:-0.5}); usplat/seg_eval.py docstring ('COVERAGE RULE (plan §3, fixed before any val run)'); scripts/eval_seg.py:563-564 (help '[A: set on Replica val]')
findings.problem: No script or report tunes tau_cov on the validation scenes. It is a fixed default of 0.5. The paper sentence says 'The coverage floor tau_cov = \ph and all temperatures are set on the validation scenes'.
findings.failure_scenario: The paper claims a validation choice that was never made. There is no leak, since the value is fixed, but the claim is false.
findings.evidence: grep of docs/ and scripts/ finds only the default 0.5 and the plan symbol list. seg_eval's docstring says the rule was fixed before any val run.
findings.fix: Write 'tau_cov = 0.5, fixed before any run; all temperatures are fit on the validation scenes'.

findings.title: The eval JSON records the wrong prompt templates
findings.problem: out['vocab']['templates'] is vocab['templates'], which load_vocab builds from the legacy 'template' key: ['a photo of a {} in a room.']. The text embeddings actually use extractor_templates(vocab, 'lseg'), the 5-template ensemble.
findings.failure_scenario: Anyone who reads eval_test.json to learn which prompts produced Table I sees one template, not the five that were used.
findings.evidence: CPU check: load_vocab(...)['templates'] -> ['a photo of a {} in a room.']; extractor_templates(v, 'lseg') -> ['a photo of a {}.', 'a photo of the {}.', 'there is a {} in the scene.', 'a photo of a {} in a room.', 'a cropped photo of a {}.'].
findings.fix: Record templates=extractor_templates(vocab, args.extractor) (and the extractor name) in out['vocab'].

findings.title: Field and map saves are not atomic and have no disk check, so a truncated file would be reused
findings.where: scripts/run_mapping.py:323 (torch.save(out, args.out)); usplat/gs_fit.py:708; scripts/replica_tab1.sh:30, 36 (reuse if the file exists); scripts/replica_tab3.sh:34-38 (set -e exits before the '|| tail' on line 38, so a mapping crash prints nothing)
findings.problem: The disk is 97% full (30 GB free) and is shared with USGLoc. If torch.save fails or is killed part-way, a partial .pt stays at the final path. The next run then skips mapping ('file exists'), and eval_seg crashes on torch.load. In replica_tab3.sh, a failed mapping call ends the script under set -e before the tail of the log is printed.
findings.failure_scenario: If USGLoc fills the disk while office_3's 1.3 GB field is being written, the test eval crashes on a truncated file. The fix and rerun also re-evaluate the scenes already done (see the finding on mid-run crashes).
findings.evidence: df: /dev/nvme0n1p1 937G, 861G used, 30G avail (97%). Field size is about 1.3 kB per Gaussian (office_0 819,126,064 B / 620,290; room_2 1,236,880,094 B / 954,119), so up to 1.32 GB per field at the 1M cap. The Table I test needs <= ~8.3 GB (6 fields + ~56 MB maps). That fits alone, but Table III variants and views fields share the disk.
findings.fix: Save to args.out + '.tmp' and then os.replace. Before each mapping call, check `df --output=avail` >= 3 GB and stop with a message if not. In replica_tab3.sh:34, add `|| { tail -20 log; exit 1; }` to the gpu_gate call itself.

findings.title: STAGE is not validated, so any value other than 'val' runs the test branch
findings.where: scripts/replica_tab1.sh:27, 50 (if [ "$STAGE" = val ] ... else <test>); the same pattern in replica_tab3.sh and replica_views.sh
findings.problem: Both branches test only for the literal 'val'. A typo or another word ('Val', 'validation', 'tset') selects the test scenes and the test evaluation.
findings.failure_scenario: After a successful val run, `STAGE=Val scripts/replica_tab1.sh` (meant as a val rerun) maps the 6 test scenes and runs the one-time test evaluation.
findings.evidence: bash check: STAGE=val -> val scenes; STAGE=Val, test, tset -> 'TEST scenes + test eval'.
findings.fix: At the top: `case "$STAGE" in val|test) ;; *) echo "STAGE must be val or test"; exit 1;; esac`. For test, also require an explicit CONFIRM_TEST=1.

findings.title: The rule that keeps the gate away from USGLoc lives in an unrecorded environment variable
findings.where: scripts/gpu_gate.sh:21, 40-44 (UAGS_GPU_USGLOC_EXTRA_MIB default 0); scripts/replica_tab1.sh (no gate env pinned)
findings.problem: The 20:18 val relaunch waited for 'free >= 109047 MiB' ('never beside a USGLoc job'). With the script defaults, the requirement would be 9000 + 2048 = 11048 MiB. So the policy came from an env var set by hand that no script or log records. TAU_COV and DOWNSCALE env overrides are also not pinned: a tau_cov mismatch only warns.
findings.failure_scenario: The test run launched from a fresh shell uses a different gate policy from the val run. It can start beside a USGLoc batch, which is the setup of the earlier OOM crashes. gpu_reserve now lowers that risk.
findings.evidence: tab1/eval_val.log: '[gpu_gate] 2026-09-29 20:18:31 waiting: free 590 MiB < 109047 or lock busy'. gpu_gate.sh required() = need + headroom (+ usgloc_extra if USGLoc is running).
findings.fix: Pin the policy in replica_tab1.sh (export UAGS_GPU_USGLOC_EXTRA_MIB=${UAGS_GPU_USGLOC_EXTRA_MIB:-99999}). Echo all UAGS_* env vars, TAU_COV and DOWNSCALE into the stage log at start. Make eval_seg refuse, not just warn, when tau_cov differs from the fit's value.

findings.title: run_mapping sets no seed; the PCA pixel subsample relies on PyTorch's implicit CUDA default seed
findings.where: usplat/feature_pca.py:34 (torch.randperm on z.device); scripts/run_mapping.py:129-173 (no torch.manual_seed in run_gsplat)
findings.problem: Each PCA frame (240x320 = 76,800 pixels) is cut to 20,000 random pixels. run_gsplat never seeds, so the basis is reproducible only if the CUDA default generator starts from a fixed seed, and no earlier CUDA random call has moved it. In this build the CPU default seed is random per process. The k-view fields of the views figure refit the PCA too, so any change in the basis adds noise to the per-pixel k-vs-full comparison.
findings.failure_scenario: The same saved command rebuilds a field with a slightly different PCA basis. The effect is small, but it is not reproducible by construction.
findings.evidence: Two CPU runs of `torch.initial_seed(), torch.randperm(76800)[:3]` gave 5031214125354848027 [51648, 24706, 34024] and 5751053207044270839 [29599, 29431, 32253]. grep finds no manual_seed in run_mapping.run_gsplat. (The CUDA default was not checked: no GPU use was allowed.)
findings.fix: Add torch.manual_seed(args.seed) (new --seed, default 0) at the start of run_gsplat, or pass a torch.Generator to StreamingPCA.accumulate. Store the seed in the field file.

findings.title: The paper never says how pixels with undefined u_ale rank in AUSE_u
findings.where: papers/main.tex sec:metrics (only uncovered pixels are described); usplat/seg_eval.py:335-360 (undefined_key: NaN ranks above every finite value)
findings.problem: For our rows, AUSE_u uses u_ale. On validation, u_ale is defined for only 84.2% / 81.8% of pixel mass, so a large share of pixels fall in the 'undefined' tier. That tier ranks above every defined value. The number therefore depends heavily on a rule the paper does not state.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader cannot reproduce or interpret ours' AUSE_u in Table I without knowing that about 16-18% of covered pixels are ranked as most uncertain because their u_ale is undefined.
findings.evidence: docs/reports/2026-09-29-replica-tab1/README.md findings row: 'defined for 22.4% / 12.2% of Gaussians but 84.2% / 81.8% of pixel mass'. seg_eval.ranking_signals uses three tiers: uncovered +inf > undefined > finite.
findings.fix: Add to sec:metrics: 'A covered pixel whose u^ale is undefined ranks above every defined value (after uncovered pixels).' Report the share of such pixels (n_undefined is already in the JSON) in the caption or text.

checked_ok: Temperatures are fit only on the val scenes: fit_on runs only with --val-scenes, the test branch passes --betas, and eval_seg refuses both at once (eval_seg.py:527-528). Every row needs its own beta or the run stops before rendering.

The extractor (LSeg) and the 5-template ensemble were chosen on val only: check_clip2d.py defaults to --scenes office_0,room_2, and no test-scene name appears in the extractor study logs. vocab templates_by_extractor.lseg is exactly check_clip2d's 'ensemble', same 5 templates in the same order. The paper's 'one ensemble of five prompt templates, chosen on the validation scenes' is correct.

LSeg text embedding is the mean of per-template unit embeddings, then renormalised (lseg.py:282-290). The text cache key includes the extractor tag and the template list. CSS mapping text uses the same lseg templates.

PCA is fit per scene on its first 20 mapping frames (Sequence_1, --pca-frames 20), with no text and no labels. The 2D row reuses the map's PCA. No test labels enter any choice except the documented query-set rule.
Query set equals the CSS mapping class set on all 8 scenes (16-28 classes). There are 0 unknown label pixels and 90 evaluation frames per scene (Sequence_2 stride 10, 240x320).
tau_cov = 0.5 and undef_frac = 0.5 are the same in val and test. check_fit_settings refuses an undef_frac mismatch.
Seeds: BetaFitter uses its own Generator seeded 0 (2000 px per val view). eval_seg's RunRecord calls set_seed(0). gs_fit seeds 0 (CPU and CUDA). eval_views sets manual_seed.

run_mapping token pre-extraction (5b21781) is equivalent to 60d7796: tokens are copied to the CPU in fp32 with no loss, then take the same upsample_tokens -> pca.project path. Keyframe selection logic, CSS vocabulary, templates and FieldConfig are unchanged. Only ms_per_keyframe_extract now times the tokens only (upsample and PCA are no longer included).

make_tables row order and labels match tab:replica. Units are correct: mIoU/Acc/ECE/AURC/AUSE x100, Brier x100, NLL in nats with 2 decimals. The AUSE_u signal names exist in the code (normlift_1-R, normlift_1-Cinter in baselines.py:243-246; css_var_top; u_ale in rows.py). AURC is the MSP ranking, as the paper says.

NormLift, averaging and viewcount share the averaging buffer, so they get identical betas (36.0027) and identical office_0 metrics (mIoU 0.2995). 'Same predictive as averaging' is true for the current code.
configs/replica_val.json and replica_test.json field and map paths match the names used in replica_tab1.sh. The script's test list matches replica_test.json (6 scenes).
Under set -euo pipefail, the grep after fit and map always matches the '[gpu_gate] ... running' line that the gate writes into the same log, so it never causes a silent exit.

Both val fields have identical mapping config (only data/ply/out/css_eval_data paths differ) and identical field_config. Both val 3DGS maps have identical fit config (only log_every differs). Mapping code is unchanged between 5b21781 and HEAD apart from gpu_reserve. The working tree is clean.
Disk: 30 GB free. The Table I test needs at most ~8.3 GB (6 fields at <= 1.32 GB at the 1M-Gaussian cap, ~1.3 kB per Gaussian measured, plus ~56 MB per map).
gpu_reserve reserves (fraction x total - 512 MiB) once. No torch.cuda.empty_cache() call exists in usplat/ or scripts/ that would release it.
tests/test_seg_eval.py: 21 passed on CPU (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='', PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1, -p no:cacheprovider). No tracked files were changed.
